input.question: how do zits form, and why does popping certain zits hurt like a bitch (lip line) and others don't (forehead)
input.ground_truth: There are different kinds of breakout. Whiteheads and blackheads are simply clogged pores; the oil in the pore is either blocked, trapping the bacteria in the pore, or it is exposed to air, where the bacteria oxidizes and forms a whitehead. A pimple, or zit, when the bacteria deeper down in the pore becomes infected and inflamed, and these can be painful. Depending on the location, you can experiences different degrees of pain. There are many more sensitive nerve endings around the lip area, so you feel so many more sensations. That's why kissing someone feels so good, and why cold sores hurt like a mutha.

response.prediction:
Okay, let me explain this in a super simple way, like I'm talking to a 5-year-old:

Zits (which are also called pimples) happen when tiny holes in your skin (called pores) get clogged. These pores get clogged with oil and dead skin cells, kind of like when you accidentally drop something into a tiny hole. Sometimes, germs (tiny, invisible yucky stuff) get stuck in there too, and that makes the area red and swollen.

Now, why does popping some zits hurt more than others? Well, it depends on where the zit is. The skin around your mouth (like your lip line) is super sensitive, which means it has lots of tiny nerves that can feel pain easily. So when you pop a zit there, it hurts more because you're touching those sensitive nerves. On the other hand, the skin on your forehead is less sensitive, so popping a zit there doesn't hurt as much. It's kind of like how your finger hurts more if you accidentally touch a sharp object than if you touch it with your arm.
